source.author: verg
source.text: Et te montosae misere in proelia Nersae, Ufens, insignem fama et felicibus armis; horrida praecipue cui gens assuetaque multo venatu nemorum, duris Aequicula glaebis.
source.text_original: Et te montosae misere in proelia Nersae, / Ufens, insignem fama et felicibus armis; / horrida praecipue cui gens assuetaque multo / venatu nemorum, duris Aequicula glaebis.
source.text_english: And they sent you, Ufens, into the battles of mountainous Nersae, renowned in fame and fortunate in arms; a wild man, above all, whose people were rugged and accustomed to the deep forests with much hunting, the Aequicolan race, hardened by stubborn clods of earth.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Omnis avet quae iam bellis spectataque fama turba ducum, primae seu quos in flore iuventae temptamenta tenent necdum data copia rerum:
reuse.text_original: Omnis avet quae iam bellis spectataque fama / turba ducum, primae seu quos in flore iuventae / temptamenta tenent necdum data copia rerum: /
reuse.text_english: All the whole crowd of leaders, already famed and tested in wars, whether those whom the first bloom of youth still holds in their first attempts and to whom no full opportunity has yet been given, longs for it.
